name: Children's ward
description: Children under 16 who need to stay in hospital, each with a fold-out bed beside them so a parent can stay the night. Run by children's nurses (one for every four beds) and a paediatric doctor.
staffing: Hire a children's nurse for every 4 beds and a paediatric doctor from Recruitment (H), posted to this ward. Adult nurses and doctors can't work here.

name: Children's HDU
description: High dependency beds for very poorly children: bad asthma, sepsis, after a big operation. A children's nurse for every two beds. Children who need intensive care go to the regional children's ICU.
staffing: Hire a children's nurse for every two beds and a paediatric doctor, posted to the unit.

name: Children's waiting room
description: A waiting room just for children and their parents, away from the adults in the main waiting room. Built empty: give it a door through to a corridor and place chairs. Children register at the main reception desk, then wait here for triage and for a cubicle.
staffing: No staff of its own: the A&E team call children through from here.

name: Children's cubicle
description: A children's A&E cubicle, brightly painted, with a chair for mum or dad. Children of any triage colour but Red are seen here first; adults never use it.
staffing: The A&E team see children here.

name: Children's assessment unit
description: A short-stay unit where children are watched for a few hours (up to 12) before going home, and where poorly children wait for a bed on the children's ward. Each bed has a fold-out bed for a parent.
staffing: A children's nurse for every 4 beds and a paediatric doctor, posted to the unit.

name: Children's intensive care (PICU)
description: Intensive care for children: ventilators and a children's nurse at every bed. It only takes children while an anaesthetist is posted to it, as well as a paediatric doctor; without one, children who need intensive care go to the regional PICU.
staffing: A children's nurse at every bed, a paediatric doctor and an anaesthetist, posted to the unit.
